predecessors.name: Sui dynasty
predecessors.text: the Sui empire, taken piecemeal from Emperor Yang's successors and the rival regimes between the occupation of Chang'an in winter 617 and the defeat of Liang Shidu in 628 ('The transition ended in…

predecessors.name: Gao Kaidao
predecessors.text: Gao Kaidao's Yan state in extreme northern Hebei: 'his Yan state was also integrated into Tang' by 624

successors.name: Later Liang
successors.text: most of the Tang heartland after Zhu Wen deposed Ai: infobox 'Abdication in favour of Later Liang: June 1, 907'

successors.name: Jin (Former Jin)
successors.text: Shanxi, Li Keyong's and Li Cunxu's Jin (Cliopatria's neighbour row; the Tang page does not describe the successors)

successors.name: Qi (Li Maozhen's state)
successors.text: Shaanxi west of the capital (Cliopatria row from 911)

successors.name: Yan (Liu Shouguang)
successors.text: northern Hebei around Youzhou (Cliopatria row from 911)

ledger.x: 618: Li Yuan proclaims the Tang at Chang'an.
618: Li Xiaogong brings the Sui cities of the south over to the Tang.
Dec 618: Li Shimin destroys Xue Rengao's Qin.
619: Li Gui's state surrenders to the Tang.
619: Liu Wuzhou takes Shanxi from the Tang.
620: Liu Wuzhou's Dingyang annexed.
620: Gao Kaidao submits to the Tang.
620: Du Fuwei's land is the Tang's.
621: Gao Kaidao rebels against the Tang.
621: Wang Shichong's Zheng annexed.
621: Xiao Xian surrenders at Jiangling.
621: Li Zitong's Wu annexed.
621: Shandong passes to the Tang.
621: Xu Yuanlang rises against the Tang.
621: Li Shimin wins at Hulao and Dou Jiande's Xia is annexed.
622: Liu Heita retakes the former Xia land.
622: Lin Shihong's Chu ends and passes to the Tang.
623: Liu Heita is betrayed and executed.
623: Xu Yuanlang is killed and the Tang take back his land.
624: Fu Gongshi's Song crushed.
624: Gao Kaidao's Yan passes to the Tang.
628: the last warlord falls.
630: the Eastern Turks fall.
630-645: the Turks as Tang vassals.
634: the Tuyuhun become a Tang vassal.
640: Gaochang conquered; the Anxi protectorate founded.
644: Karasahr taken.
645: the buffer khaganate ends with the Tang reconquest; Chebi Khan's revival attempt (646-650) fails.
1 August 646: the Tang and the Uyghurs destroy the Xueyantuo.
647: the steppe submits; the Yanran protectorate founded.
648: Kucha falls; the Four Garrisons.
648: Kucha conquered.
657: the Western Turks fall; the Tang at its largest.
660: Baekje destroyed.
661: the lands west of the Pamirs as Tang clients.
663: the Tuyuhun fall to Tibet (tibetan-empire takes the land).
666: the Western Turks under Tang overlordship.
ledger.cpn: Western Turks after the Tang conquest (Cliopatria 'Turks')

ledger.x: 668: Goguryeo destroyed; the Protectorate General to Pacify the East at Pyongyang.
670: the Four Garrisons fall to Tibet.
670: the Silla-Tang War begins.
671: Silla drives the Tang out of most of Baekje.
673: the Tang retake Qiuci.
674: the Dzungaria piece enters the same Tang overlordship.
ledger.cpn: Western Turks after the Tang conquest (Cliopatria 'Turks')

ledger.x: 676: the war ends in Silla's favour.
676: Korea south of the Taedong passes to Silla.
677: Duzhi's rebellion ends the Tang overlordship over the Chu and Zhetysu lands.
ledger.cpn: Western Turks after the Tang conquest (Cliopatria 'Turks')

ledger.x: 677: the Dzungaria piece leaves the Tang overlordship with Duzhi's declaration: his own tribes are the Wuduolu Turks of Dzungaria whom the Tang had assigned to him.
ledger.cpn: Western Turks after the Tang conquest (Cliopatria 'Turks')

ledger.x: 677: Tibet takes Qiuci again.
679: the Tarim recovered.
682: the steppe is lost to the Second Turkic Khaganate.

c. 682: the Pyongyang district leaves the Tang map. 'Silla failed to regain the former Goguryeo territories north of the Taedong River, which were now under Tang dominion', yet the Andong seat had been 'moved to the Old City of Liaodong' in the second month of 676 and to Xincheng in 677…
687: the Tarim lost again.
690: Wu Zetian proclaims the Zhou.
690: the capital is Luoyang, renamed Shendu (Divine Capital).
692: Wang Xiaojie recovers the Four Garrisons.

c. 705: the Tang lose the Goguryeo heartland east of Liaodong, where Balhae rises. 'Parhae was founded in 698 by Tae Choyong', after 'three Mohe chieftains took advantage of the Khitan rebellion to move further east' in 696; the Balhae dossier has the state grow to the Cliopatria 705 outline at the same…
705: the Tang restored.
705: the court returns to Chang'an.
714: the Andong protectorate leaves Liaodong.
719: the Turgesh capture Suyab.
738: Nanzhao recognised as a Tang tributary.
751: Nanzhao breaks with the Tang.
July 751: the Battle of Talas; the abbasid-caliphate takes the Tang's place in Transoxiana.
755: An Lushan rebels.
755-763: the An Lushan rebellion's fighting zone (rule 6 blend where neither side holds firmly).
756: Luoyang falls to the rebels.
756: Chang'an falls.
757: the capitals recovered.
759: Luoyang falls again.
762: Luoyang recovered.
763: Tibet takes Yanqi.
763: the An Lushan rebellion ends.
763: Hebei returns to the Tang in name.
763: Tibet in Chang'an.
763: the Tibetans leave Chang'an after fifteen days.
764: Tibet takes Liangzhou and cuts off the west.
764-783: the Tang-Tibetan war for Longyou and Hexi after the An Lushan rebellion.
783: a treaty defines the Tang-Tibetan borders.
787: Kucha falls.

c. 790: the protectorates end. 'the last vestiges of the protectorate and its garrisons were defeated by Tibetan forces by 790'. The page dates Beiting's creation (702) and its isolation (764) but not its end, so 790 for Beiting itself, and Dzungaria and Turfan…
792: Khotan falls, the last garrison.
794: Nanzhao returns to the Tang.
803: Champa seizes Nghe An from the Tang.
809: the Tang recover Nghe An.
848: Zhang Yichao rises at Dunhuang.
850: the corridor recovered.
851: 'In 851 Zhang captured Xizhou (Gaochang).'
851: the Guiyi Circuit.
861: Guiyi's authority extends to Liangzhou 'and several other prefectures, including Lanzhou, Hezhou, and Kuozhou'.
863: Nanzhao takes Annam.
866: Annam recovered.
866: Xizhou (Gaochang) is lost to the Uyghurs of Qocho.
876: Yizhou (Hami) is lost.
881: Huang Chao takes Chang'an.
883: Chang'an retaken.
902: Nanzhao ends.
904: the court moved to Luoyang.
904: Zhang Chengfeng retakes Yizhou and Xizhou.
907: Zhu Wen ends the Tang.
907: the Tang ends and the Guiyi Circuit carries on alone.

wars.name: Tang campaign against the Eastern Turks
wars.outcome: Tang victory: Illig Qaghan captured in 630 and the khaganate overthrown; the Ashina settled in the Ordos Loop as vassals (buffer state 639-645, reconquered 645).

wars.name: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks
wars.outcome: Tang victory; fall of the Western Turkic Khaganate in 657 and the Tang's largest extent.

wars.name: Goguryeo–Tang War and the fall of Baekje
wars.outcome: Baekje toppled in 660 by a Tang-Silla invasion (Tang page) and Goguryeo destroyed by 668; the Protectorate General to Pacify the East was set up and 'based in Pyongyang'.

wars.name: Silla–Tang War
wars.outcome: Silla victory: Silla controls the Korean peninsula south of the Taedong River (Baekje from 671, the rest in 676), the Tang keep Liaodong and the Goguryeo land north of it; the Andong seat retreats to Liaoyang (676) and Xincheng (677); the page records a…

wars.name: Tang–Tibetan war for the Four Garrisons
wars.outcome: Tibet takes Qiuci and the Tarim in 670 (Dafei River), the Tang retake it in 673, Tibet in 677, the Tang again in 679, the Tang withdraw in 686 and Tibet establishes control in 687; Wang Xiaojie recovers it for the Tang in 692 and the Anxi Protectorate is…

wars.name: Tang–Nanzhao war
wars.outcome: Tang defeated at Xiaguan in 751; Li Mi's 754 army 'never made it past Mu'ege'; Nanzhao allied with Tibet from 754 to 794.

wars.name: Battle of Talas
wars.outcome: Abbasid victory in July 751; 'Consolidation of Abbasid rule in Transoxania; End of Tang presence in Transoxania', but 'no significant loss or gain of territory occurred and the borders remained relatively unchanged'; the Tang recovered Little and Great Balur…

wars.name: An Lushan rebellion
wars.outcome: Tang victory on 17 February 763 (Shi Chaoyi's suicide), with Uyghur assistance in the recapture of Chang'an and Luoyang in late 757; the Western Regions lost 'most of its control' to troop withdrawal, and 'three fanzhen became virtually independent' in Hebei.

wars.name: Tang–Tibetan war after the An Lushan rebellion
wars.outcome: Tibet captured Chang'an for fifteen days in November 763, took Liang Prefecture in 764 and cut off the Anxi and Beiting protectorates; a 783 treaty defined the borders; the garrisons fall in 787-792 (Anxi page).

wars.name: Nanzhao's campaigns against the Tang
wars.outcome: Annam lost in 863 and retaken by Gao Pian in fall 866; the Sichuan campaigns held no ground; Shilong's death in 877 'effectively ended Nanzhao's expansionist campaigns'.

wars.name: Huang Chao rebellion
wars.outcome: Chang'an retaken by Li Keyong in summer 883; Huang Chao killed on 13 July 884; the rebellion 'permanently destroyed the power of the Tang dynasty'.

wars.name: Transition from Sui to Tang (Tang unification wars)
wars.outcome: Tang victory over every rival: Qin (618), Liang of Hexi (619), Dingyang (620), Xia and Zheng at Hulao (621), Liang of Xiao Xian (621), Wu (621), Liu Heita (623), Song (624), Gao Kaidao's Yan (624), Liang Shidu (628).

certainty.note: The steppe, Tarim and Tibetan frontiers are approximate; the provincial frontiers in the south follow Tang circuits; the Korean frontier is the Taedong River from 676 (Silla-Tang page).
The Tibetan frontier is sharp from the 783 treaty that 'defined the borders' (Tibetan Empire page) and the 821/822 treaty until the Tibetan collapse of 842-848; every other frontier stays soft.
